title: Our Present Affects Their Future
author: Ryan Holiday
summary: This Daily Dad meditation sets Theodore Roosevelt and Rudyard Kipling side by side as the two writers who most beautifully celebrated conquest, adventure, war and empire. Both ended up grieving sons, Quentin Roosevelt shot down over France and Jack Kipling lost in the trenches in 1915 so completely that his body was never identified. The author argues that the two men were not blameless, both because of the pressure they put on their children and because they belonged to a generation that cheered and glibly supported the policies that led to the carnage. He widens it into a cautionary tale for every parent, since each generation makes present decisions whose consequences fall mainly on the next. The future generations affected are not faceless hordes but our own children and grandchildren. The closing challenge is to consider what we cheerlead, rationalize or ignore today, because our kids will live in the world those choices create.
points: Roosevelt and Kipling, celebrants of war and empire, each lost a son to the conflict, which the piece uses as a warning about the cost of glorifying it.
The author holds that the two fathers were not blameless, since they pressured their children and encouraged the policies that led to the war.
Decisions made in the present have consequences borne mainly by future generations, who are our own children and grandchildren rather than abstractions.
Parents are asked to examine the culture wars, short-term policies and ignored warning signs they tolerate, because their kids will inherit the results.
quotes: Theodore Roosevelt lost his son Quentin, shot down over France. Kipling lost his son Jack in the trenches in 1915, so destroyed by ‘shot and shell’ that they never identified the body.

But it’s also indisputable that these two great men were not blameless in bringing them about—not only because of the pressure and impossible expectations they put on their children, but because they were part of a generation that had encouraged, celebrated, glibly supported the policies that led to the carnage that claimed their sons.
Our generation, just as all past generations have, make decisions in the present that have consequences borne primarily by future generations.
But these future generations are not faceless, nameless hordes, they are our children and grandchildren.
Just as your children will reap the natural extrapolations of what you cheerlead or rationalize or pay no attention to today.

The culture wars you get caught up in, the dunking you enjoy, the short term policies you support, the warning signs you ignore? Your kids and your grandkids will live in the world they create...and you yourself may live long enough for it to break your heart.
